newsitem.title: JAPAN: Forex reforms will not weaken monetary policy - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Forex reforms will not weaken monetary policy - BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday that planned reforms of Japan's foreign exchange controls are not likely to weaken the effectiveness of the central bank's monetary policy.

Matsushita was responding to a question as to whether the foreign exchange control revisions would encourage business transaction settlements among Japanese companies in foreign currencies and if this would undermine the effectiveness of the BOJ's monetary policy.
Matsushita said he does not think Japanese companies would transfer substantial yen settlements into foreign currencies.
"I don't think the effectiveness of Japan's monetary policy will be weakened after the planned reforms of foreign exchange regulations," he said.
The reforms are expected to take place in the fiscal year beginning March 1998.
